overview: This bill creates the Endless Mountains National Heritage Area in northeastern Pennsylvania, covering Bradford, Sullivan, Susquehanna, and Wyoming counties, plus parts of other counties identified in an earlier feasibility study, with exact boundaries set by the Interior Department. A national heritage area is a region recognized for its history, culture, and landscape, where a local organization works with the National Park Service to promote and preserve those resources; the land stays in private or local hands. Endless Mountains Heritage Region, Inc. would manage the area and must submit a management plan to the Interior Department within three years. Federal assistance for the area would end 15 years after the bill becomes law. As of September 17, 2026, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate calendar for possible floor action.
for: Supporters say national recognition and modest federal support would help this rural region promote its history and outdoor attractions, boosting tourism and local preservation.
against: Critics say heritage areas add to ongoing federal costs while the National Park Service has a large maintenance backlog, and that leaving the boundaries to be set later creates uncertainty for residents.
